title: Ottawa to indefinitely extend MAID exclusion for people solely suffering from mental illness
summary: The federal government will introduce legislation this fall that will indefinitely extend the ban on access to a medically assisted death for people who are only suffering from a mental illness,…

image.caption: Minister of Justice Sean Fraser says the government will soon table legislation with its changes to medically assisted death. (Justin Tang/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: The federal government will introduce legislation this fall that will indefinitely extend the ban on access to a medically assisted death for people who are only suffering from a mental illness, Justice Minister Sean Fraser said on Wednesday.
Justice minister says legislation will be introduced this fall

"Canada has made a decision not to move forward with the expansion that is scheduled in the Criminal Code of medical assistance in dying in circumstances where mental illness is the sole basis," he said in the foyer of the House of Commons.
Fraser said the government's decision reflects the position expressed by a special parliamentary committee report released in June along with his own department's probing of the issue.

Government to reveal next steps for medically assisted dying

blocks.text: "While there is not a perfect consensus on this issue, we believe this is the correct approach at this particular time," he said.

Fraser said the promised legislation will also "open the door" for people to give advance consent for their own medically assisted death in circumstances where the illness they are suffering from will eventually eliminate their capacity to make that decision.

The minister explained that while the details of advance consent will be worked out in House of Commons committees, it will require a person's illness to be incurable and result in intolerable suffering.

Peter Zimonjic is a senior writer for CBC News who reports for digital, radio and television. He has worked as a reporter and columnist in London, England, for the Telegraph, Times and Daily Mail, and in Canada for the Ottawa Citizen, Torstar and Sun Media. He is the author of Into The Darkness: An Account of 7/7, published by Vintage.
